title: Doty and Lear spread quackery around the Majestic 12 era

tellings.quote:

plain: In the 1980s, Michels says, the story of the MJ-12 documents (papers that surfaced then describing a secret group set up under Truman to deal with UFOs) was pushed along with "all sorts of quackery." He says counterintelligence people like Richard Doty, an agent of the Air Force Office of Special Investigations, were saying there were six alien beings, and that a man named John Lear claimed there was "a soul catcher on the moon." Michels tells this in his own framing, as part of how he thinks the real questions got buried under wild claims.
